No user-visible intentional differences remain.

deepQaSummary.adversarialPasses: Two adversarial passes. The first caught a HIGH silent no-op in the #12 server override (wrong column s.name vs the real name_en, masked by a test fixture; fixed #83) and a MEDIUM latent /api/lines position collision (fixed #84). The second reviewed the fixes clean. A deep 7-state user-visible #9/#11 analysis then caught a HARD phantom-rows defect (server airport-only guard used non-existent ids) and a soft rounding gap, both fixed #89.
deepQaSummary.serverFixesDeployGated: #12 short-turn destinations, #9 phantom-rows + rounding are correct + test-verified but take effect only on the next Pi deploy (deploy.sh, SSH to the LAN Pi, which the sandbox safety layer blocks). Production endpoint verified: currently serves the pre-fix behaviour (M1 last train -> Kifissia, 0 lastTrains).

features.expected: One source-selection policy (local-first for Athens)
features.note: A deep 7-state user-visible analysis (fresh/stale/down server x cache present/missing x remote/seed newer) found the architectural local-first (iOS) vs server-first (Android/Web) split produces at most a data-version-skew difference behind an identical chip in rare states - iOS deliberately stays local-first for Athens to avoid a drifted/spoofed server clock overwriting a correct offline answer, so this is a defensible design difference, not a bug. It DID surface two concrete rider-facing defects, both fixed in #89: (1) HARD - the server airport-only guard used non-existent ids M3_PEK/M3_KRP instead of M3_PEA/M3_KO2, so Android/Web showed phantom 'towards Doukissis Plakentias' rows at Peania-Kantza/Koropi that iOS never showed; (2) SOFT - the server rounded banker's while all three clients round half-up, a <=1 min disagreement on half-integer-headway slots. Remaining known limitation (post-2.0 fast-follow, edge case): web shows no departures on a true offline cold-start (no bundled per-line band seed, unlike iOS/Android). Server fixes are deploy-gated on the Pi (same path as #12).

features.expected: LIVE->SCHEDULED fallback wired as first tier (X93-97 live ETAs)
features.note: External blocker + tied to #9. LiveArrivalsRouter and its providers are built AND Koin-registered (DomainModule), but nothing resolves the router (no consumer), and GetNextDeparturesUseCase does not take it. OASA endpoint is configured (api-syrmos.peterdsp.dev/api/oasa-airport-buses); the two other providers are intentional null placeholders (no operator feed exists). Wiring it is a source-policy change (#9) whose only live path depends on the Pi endpoint actually serving X93-97 data (unverifiable from CI). Deliberately not wired for GA.

features.expected: One confidence rule shared by all clients
features.note: COSMETIC, not a rider-facing defect (confirmed by the deep analysis): for the SAME train at the SAME time the displayed time and destination are identical across platforms; only the confidence CHIP wording differs offline (iOS 'Scheduled', Android 'Estimated', Web 'Offline snapshot'). Online all three agree ('Scheduled'). No rider is directed to a wrong train by the chip. iOS's blanket .scheduled is the outlier (arguably should say estimated offline) but is not misdirecting. Left as a deliberate soft/labeling difference; unifying it is optional polish, not a correctness fix.

features.expected: Short-turn last-train destination override in the shared projector
features.note: Fixed server-side. project_next_departures now applies the last_train_endpoints short-turn override (M1 00:30 -> Omonia, not Kifissia). Android and Web are server-first so they inherit it with no client change; iOS was already correct via its synced bundle. NOTE: the adversarial pass caught that the initial fix (#80) queried a nonexistent stations.name column (production has name_en/name_el), so the OperationalError guard swallowed it and the override was a silent no-op in production; #83 corrects it to name_en and rebuilds the test fixture to mirror the production schema so a wrong column now fails the tests. Offline (bundled seed ships zero short-turn rows) every platform shows the line terminal, consistent. Deploy note: takes effect once the Pi applies migration 0017 and the STASY scraper populates the table; a verified no-op until then. The KMP/Web client fallback band-projectors do NOT mirror the override yet (a documented fast-follow, no-op offline since the seed is empty).

features.classification: PARITY VERIFIED - IMPLEMENTATION-ONLY DIFFERENCE (not a user-visible intentional difference)
features.note: The rider sees the same train in the same place at the same wall-clock. Vehicle motion is driven by CADisplayLink on iOS (native, display-synced), a per-tick coroutine on Compose/Android, and requestAnimationFrame on web; all three interpolate the SAME projected positions along the SAME shapes, so user-visible behaviour is equivalent. Matching engines is neither possible (no CADisplayLink on Android/web) nor better. Under the user-visible-behaviour rule this is NOT a parity difference and should not be counted as an intentional user-visible difference; it is an implementation detail. (A minor map-padding tweak remains cosmetic backlog.)
